newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan navy ordered to pay record compensation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan navy ordered to pay record compensation.

text.p: A Taiwan court on Wednesday ordered the navy to pay T$170 million (US$6.15 million) to an insurance company over an incident in 1994 in which a civilian plane was accidentally shot down, killing four people.
It would be the largest compensatory amount the military was ever ordered to pay, naval officials said, adding that the decision would be appealed.

"The navy must take responsibility over the tragedy and pay a total of T$170.84 million in compensation to the Taiwan Fire and Marine Insurance Company," said the order handed down by the Taipei district court.

The accident occurred on September 17, 1994, during rehearsals for a major military exercise in eastern Taiwan when a naval frigate fired an anti-aircraft missile at the civilian plane, which was towing a traget drone.
All four crew aboard the plane died.

The Learjet-35, leased to the navy by the private Golden Eagle Airlines, was towing the target plane in a public rehearsal for the exercises. It exploded into flames and plunged into the sea before 3,000 political and military leaders and other dignitaries.

Investigations showed the frigate's captain improperly used a hand signal to give the order to fire instead of a verbal commanding, confusing the crew members in charge of launching the missile, the verdict said.
Golden Eagle later sought compensation from the insurance company, which in turn filed a suit against the navy.
